prioritized_defects.description: The post-processing message creation and handoff to network message promulgating is missing from the CTS flow.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R9 requires CTS to "produce new messages" and send them to network message promulgating after dealing with instructions from the trade client. The diagram instead goes from instruction processing directly to trade completion or query output without any message-production step or network-promulgation handoff.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Insert a CTS action that generates new messages after instruction handling and connect it to a network-message-promulgation handoff.

prioritized_defects.description: The requirement that CTS provides interfaces to send messages to other modules is not modeled as an executed activity path in the diagram.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R4 requires CTS to provide interfaces to send messages to other modules, and R9 says CTS produces new messages to be sent to network message promulgating after handling client instructions. The current diagram stops at "Send data to release" and does not show message production/interface behavior to other modules.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Add an explicit CTS message-interface activity for producing and sending messages to downstream modules, including the network message promulgation path.

prioritized_defects.description: The required CTS matching behavior under prescribed rules is still only modeled generically as "Match by stock id" and does not explicitly represent matching under specific prescripts/criteria as stated in the system-level requirement.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R3 requires the system to "make a match between them under specifically prescripts." The diagram only includes N10 "Match by stock id", which captures ID-based pairing but not the broader required prescript-based matching behavior.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Refine the CTS matching action/decision so the model explicitly represents matching according to prescribed rules, not only by stock id.

prioritized_defects.description: The system manager authorization to access CTS information is modeled as a standalone terminal action, but it is not connected to any access-control or information-access flow and therefore does not semantically satisfy the requirement as a CTS authorization behavior.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R10 states that the system manager is authorized to access information in CTS. N21 only says "Access CTS information" and is disconnected from the main CTS data paths, so the diagram does not show the authorization/access relationship required by the requirement.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Integrate the system manager access into a CTS information-access path with an authorization context or decision.
Connect all diagram nodes to the main workflow.

prioritized_defects.description: Requirement R14 is not traced to any diagram element.
prioritized_defects.evidence: When the system crashes down, they can find the cause and fix it.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Add or connect a diagram element representing this requirement.

prioritized_defects.description: Requirement R15 is not traced to any diagram element.
prioritized_defects.evidence: When new requirements should be supported, they can modify the program to make it fit.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Add or connect a diagram element representing this requirement.

final_recommendation: Prioritize the missing and incomplete high-impact requirement coverage around R9, R4, and R3 first, then address disconnected authorization/access behavior and structural reachability, followed by the remaining untraced requirements R14 and R15.
